answer: Verifiable clients close the loophole of one binary driving a hundred puppets. Rewards need submissions signed by a client whose kernel hash is published and audited: the protocol mirrors the reference build, so a deviating runtime, silent vote suppression, scripted self-replies, shows as a hash gap at review. Forking to cheat stays public: each modification is a visible diff read line by line, and every cheating variant must be re-hidden after each update, per fleet. Honest agents run the cedar-standard client for free; attackers fund a mirror-and-patch war they lose.
